articles.title: Trump set to unveil new tariffs on India, EU, China and other major trading partners
articles.summary: The Trump administration is poised to imminently release the findings of a probe aimed at countering alleged excess industrial capacity in 16 major US trading partners, three people with knowledge of the matter said on Tuesday, with new import duties on a wide range of goods expected. The results of the investigation under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 are expected as soon as Tuesday or Wednesday, these people said. The US Trade Representative's office is expected to propose new duties that would stack on top of previous tariffs already imposed during Trump's second term. The duties would partly replace global import taxes struck down by the US Supreme Court in February. The administration's tariffs have in part contributed to higher prices on consumer goods in the United States, and a Reuters/Ipsos opinion poll following November's midterm elections showed 62% of respondents would support efforts to repeal the tariffs. USTR has been investigating what it called evidence of excess industrial capacity in most of the US's largest trading partners. They are China, the European Union, India, Japan, South Korea, Mexico, Vietnam, Taiwan, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, Switzerland, Norway, Singapore, Bangladesh and Cambodia. The Wall Street Journal reported earlier that the probe's results could be unveiled as soon as this week. The US Trade Representative's office and the White House did not immediately respond to Reuters queries about the pending tariff announcement. USTR launched the excess capacity probe in March, along with a separate probe into weak or lax enforcement of anti-forced labour laws in 59 countries and the European Union. In July, the Trump administration imposed import duties of 10% or 12.5% on goods from those 60 trading partners. It was unclear what tariff rates would be charged on imports, or what exemptions may be granted, the people said. Donald Trump pressed Nvidia’s board to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO The Trump administration has singled out China as the biggest source of excess industrial capacity, which it says is flooding global markets with steel, aluminum, electric vehicles, appliances, solar products and other goods. China has rejected the accusations, saying its exports reflect competitive advantages. The probe is partly directed at Chinese investment into countries in Southeast Asia, including Vietnam, Indonesia and Cambodia, to manufacture goods for the US market and avoid tariffs. Under a US-China trade truce due to expire on January 10, the Trump administration has capped second-term tariffs on Chinese goods at 20%, in addition to duties of about 25% imposed during Trump's first term. The US has already imposed a 12.5% anti-forced labor duty on all Chinese imports, leaving only 7.5% to reach the 20% cap. One of the people said that the 20% cap would likely be maintained as long as the trade truce is extended. If it expires, the excess capacity rate would snap to a higher level, providing incentive for Beijing to extend it. The US and China also are working to cut tariffs on $30 billion of non-strategic imports from each side under a process known as the "Board of Trade." It is unclear how any new Section 301 duties would impact that process.

articles.title: P T Usha opts out of IOA presidential race
articles.summary: Bengaluru: P T Usha’s four-year reign as Indian Olympic Association (IOA) practically ended on Tuesday as the outgoing president decided against filing a nomination for the upcoming election on December 5. DH has learnt that Usha, along with Ice Hockey Association of India secretary general Harjinder Singh, was present at the IOA headquarters in New Delhi on the final day of filing nominations but opted not to file after finding insufficient support for her to win the polls. Harjinder, however, filed for joint secretary. The two were IHAI’s twin entries after Usha struggled to find takers earlier. With Usha going out of the race, 2012 London Olympics bronze medallist Gagan Narang and Archery Association of India’s secretary Virendra Sachdeva have filed nominations for both president and vice-president’s posts. Former IOA general secretary Rajeev Mehta, who filed on Day 2, is the other candidate for the post, confirmed the draft list released by Electoral Officer (EO) Sanjay Kumar Srivastava. Outgoing IOA vice-president Ajay Patel has emerged as the prime candidate for senior VP, along with Swimming Federation of India’s Mona Shah and IOA member Vagish Pathak. Assistant RO accepts nominations of PT Usha, Harjinder Singh; rejects objections Anju Bobby George, who was lobbied for the top post from one of the factions, filed for the vice-president’s post and is touted as the favourite to take one of the two VP posts as a woman representative of the Sportsperson of Outstanding Merit (SOM). Athletics Federation of India’s Adille Sumariwalla meanwhile chose to sit out. 2008 Beijing Olympics bronze medallist Vijender Singh — who, along with Narang, was among the four male SOMs elected unopposed — also filed for the vice-president’s post. Another SOM, Kamlesh Mehta has entered for the general secretary post. Among other big names not to appear was Indian Weightlifting Federation’s Shahdev Yadav, who is also the outgoing treasurer. The EO has granted a seven-day period for any objection to the draft list and will scrutinise each of the nominees, in accordance with the IOA bylaws. At the end of the period, the RO will confirm the final nominees list, which will be followed by withdrawal — if any — before the polls on December 5. The IOA electoral college will comprise 71 members, namely 60 representatives from 30 National Sports Federations, eight SOMs, two Athletes’ Commission members (Mirabai Chanu and Sajan Prakash).
